questions.question: Economic planning in India is in _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Concurrent list.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__.​​**

__
 
• Economic planning is in the Concurrent List (List III) of the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution comprises three lists, which are Union, Concurrent and State lists.
 
• 
 
Concurrent List:

 
 
• It has **52 subjects** enumerated under it.
 
• The concept of ‘**Concurrent List**’ in the Indian Constitution has been borrowed from the **Constitution of Australia.**
 
• Central Government and State Government both can make laws on the subjects mentioned under the Concurrent List.
 
• However, **in case of any conflict, the law made by the Central Government prevails.​**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• 
 
Union List:

 
 
• ​Originally had **97 subjects. Now, it has 100 subjects**.
 
• The Union List **signifies the strong centre **as it has more subjects than the state list.
 
• The Center has **exclusive powers** to make laws on the subjects mentioned under the Union List of the Indian Constitution.​
 
 
 
• 
 
State List:

 
 
• It has** 61 subjects. Earlier, it had 66 subjects.**
 
• The laws can be made on the subjects enumerated under the State List of the Indian Constitution exclusively by the State legislatures.
 
• **Article 249 **gives Parliament the power to legislate concerning a subject enumerated in the State List in the national interest.

questions.question: Which of the following is related to the Tinkathia Pratha?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Champaran.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Champaran Satyagraha**

 
 
• **Tinkathia System or Tinkathia Pratha** was a system under which the native peasants of **Champaran.**
 
• Champaran Satyagraha was started by **Mahatma Gandhi in 1917** to look into the problem of the Tinkathia system in which peasants of Champaran were** forced to grow Indigo on 3/20th of the total land.**
 
• **Raj Kumar Shukla** persuaded Gandhi to look into the peasant's problem.
 
• Champaran Satyagraha was Mahatma Gandhi’s** first experiment of Satyagraha.**
 
• **Rajendra Prasad, J.B Kripalni, Mahadeo Desai and Narhari Parekh** joined Gandhi in the movement. 
 
• It was undertaken in the erstwhile undivided Champaran district in northern **Bihar in April 1917.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kheda Satyagraha**

 
 
• **1918** was a year of failed crops in the** Kheda district of Gujarat **due to droughts.
 
• As per law, the farmers were entitled to remission if the produce was less than a quarter of the normal output.
 
• But the** government refused any remission from paying land revenue.**
 
• **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel**, under** Gandhi’s** guidance, led the farmers in protest against the collection of taxes in the wake of the famine.
 
• The protest was peaceful and people showed remarkable courage even in the face of adversities like confiscation of personal property and arrest.
 
• Finally, the authorities gave in and gave some concessions to the farmers.

questions.question:
How CNG is a cleaner fuel?

I. It produces oxides of Sulphur and Nitrogen in very small amounts.

II. It makes environment less polluted.

III. It emits less greenhouse gases.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**All I, II and III.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Compressed Natural Gas** or **CNG** is a **clean-burning fuel**.
 
• It is the cleanest of all the fossil fuels since** it produces oxides of Sulphur and Nitrogen in very small amounts. Hence, the statement I is correct.**
 
• It also **emits fewer greenhouse gases and makes the environment less polluted. Hence, statement II and III are also correct.**
 
• It is composed of **methane** which when burnt **produces water vapours and carbon dioxide.**

questions.question: In a compound, the elements are always present in definite proportions by _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__mass__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The law of definite proportions was stated by Proust as “In a chemical substance the elements are always present in definite proportions by mass”.
 
• And the law of definite proportion does not depend on its source and preparation method.
 
 
• For example, in a compound such as water, the ratio of the mass of hydrogen to the mass of oxygen is always 1:8, whatever the source of water.
 
 
 
• Thus, if 9 g of water is decomposed, 1 g of hydrogen and 8 g of oxygen are always obtained. 
 
• Similarly, nitrogen and hydrogen are always present in the 14:3 mass ratio in ammonia, whatever the preparation method or the source from which it is produced.

questions.question: Which of the following is a CORRECT relation of length of small intestines of an herbivore and a carnivore?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Herbivore > Carnivore**__

__**Explanation:**__

__
 
• Herbivores are animals that derive energy from just eating plants, whereas carnivores are those animals which derive their energy by eating meat or flesh of other animals.
 
• The small intestine of herbivores is longer in length than carnivores since plant matter is lower in nutrients and is tough to break as compared to animal matter. Therefore, animals who are herbivores need to be efficient digesters so that they can get the necessary amount of nutrients.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Herbivores (Herb=plant, vore= to eat)**
 
• A herbivore is an animal that gets its energy from eating plants and only plants.
 
• A herbivore is an animal anatomically and physiologically adapted to eating plant materials.
 
• Many herbivores have special digestive systems that let them digest all kinds of plants, including grasses.
 
• For example foliage or marine algae, for the main component of its diet.
 
• As a result of their plant diet, herbivorous animals typically have mouthparts adapted to rasping or grinding.
 
• A carnivore is a species that feeds on killing and eating other animals.
 
• Carnivores usually consume herbivores, although they also consume omnivores.
 
• Animals that consume other animals, such as carnivores and omnivores, are vital to every environment, as they prevent other organisms from being overpopulated.
 
• Carnivores are the third trophic level. Omnivores, beings that consume a large range of species, from plants to animals to fungi, are also at the third trophic level.

questions.question: Limbs of frog, lizard, bird and human are example of ________ organs.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is__** Homologous.**__

__**Explanation:**__

 
• Limbs of frogs, lizards, birds and humans are examples of homologous organs.
 
• If the traits of two different organisms have been inherited from common ancestry, then that is known as homology.
 
• Since the arm of a human, the wings of birds and bats, and the forelimbs of frogs and lizards have a common underlying anatomy that they inherited from their last common ancestors, that is why they are known as homologous organs.

questions.question: Increased wind speed is accompanied by a reduced air ________.
questions.solution:

**__Explanation:__**

When the pressure around an area decreases, then the wind speed increases and vice versa. The higher would be the pressure difference, the more would be the wind speed. This derives 2 major concepts:

• The air always travels from high to low pressure areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Bullets**

__
 
• In Microsoft Word, bullets are small dots, squares, dashes, or graphics that are often seen before the text.
 
• The bulleted tab is located in the Paragraph group of the **Home tab**.
 
• There are a total of **8 types **of default bullets present in **MS Word 2019.** If "None" is not counted then 7 types.
 
• The bulleted tab has different types of bullet styles that can apply to a document.
 
• There are eight formats in the bulleted tab, with the top-left format being "None." 
 
• Collectively these eight formats are known as a **"gallery."**
 
• To change your style of bullet, press** ALT+ENTER** to bring up the properties box.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indentation**- Number of blank spaces or distance used to separate a paragraph from the right or left margins
 
• **Numbering-** The fastest way to get numbers for your document.
 
• **Tabs-** Placed on the ruler to control the placement of text.
